newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500 futures finish sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500 futures finish sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures shrugged off early losses by midday and rallied in the afternoon to end at the highest price since last Thursday.
Strong manufacturing data initially kept bulls at bay, but June S&Ps crawled up from early moderate losses to rally sharply amid afternoon dealer and local buying, traders said.

June poked through sticky resistance near 760.00 and set off buy stops above 762.00, 765.00 and 766.00, propelling the contract as high as 769.30. A recovery from steep losses in Nasdaq 100 futures and a constructive Treasury bond futures close aided S&P momentum, traders said.

"The Nasdaq above 800 helped, and with bonds out of the way they really took off," one S&P 500 futures trader said. She noted that bonds "didn't have a bad showing for the day," closing down 5/32 in June futures after sharp losses early.
June S&Ps "held up real well early in the session and all it took was for the bonds to come back a little bit for us to rally it," another trader said.
He said funds were noted buyers for a second consecutive session.
The rally helped June S&P 500 futures erase the last bit of Friday's losses, a day that saw a new low for the year.
Robust manufacturing data set the early bearish bond tone and stirred up talk that the Federal Reserve would raise rates again when its policy arm meets in May.
When June T-bonds were sharply lower on the data, June S&Ps did not reflect the magnitude of the bond losses and traded moderately lower but rangebound.

U.S. March industrial production was reported up 0.9 percent, above the average forecast and higher than February's revised 0.6 percent gain. March capacity use rose to 84.1 percent, the highest rate in two years, from a revised 83.6 in February.

At the close, June S&P 500 futures were up 8.60 points at 768.30, Nasdaq 100s were up 2.00 points to 809.00, Russell 2000s were down 0.05 point at 343.60, KCBT Value Line futures rose 2.65 points to 691.00, Nikkei 225 index futures were flat at 18,080.0 and Midcap 400s gained 0.50 points to 254.00.
